components.name: Native primary action
components.description: Schematic documentation preview, not the actual native implementation. Native large capsule borderedProminent action. Its wrapping ShieldActionLabel has a 52-point minimum, names working state, stacks the spinner at accessibility sizes, and returns to primary foreground when disabled. Add number uses its full-width bottom action as Done while editing, then Save number after editing; failed responses remain unconfirmed, with a successful iPhone Contacts save distinguished from a failed Shield update. Pause message remains usable during the separate mark-played update. Leaving, scene inactivity, person changes, and permission loss invalidate pending audio requests; stale results do not restart playback. Audio-session transitions are serialized and stale cleanup is ignored. The Forwarding Contacts step uses Save Shield. Source: Design/ShieldComponents.swift, Features/Settings/AddNumberView.swift, Features/Calls/CallDetailView.swift, Features/Calls/MessageAudioSession.swift, and Features/Settings/Forwarding/ForwardingActions.swift. Browser pixels, symbols, and interaction states are illustrative; SwiftUI remains authoritative.

components.name: Four native tabs
components.description: Schematic documentation preview, not the actual native implementation. Native TabView destinations Home, Calls, Messages, More. Messages combines Voicemail and Saved notice. Home explicitly uses a large native title, a grouped-color navigation background, and automatic visibility: continuous grouped canvas at rest, opaque matching background when collapsed. At accessibility sizes person context moves from the toolbar into a wrapping page section. Changing the person stops audio and dismisses the old call detail. Preview buttons show selection only and do not navigate. Source: App/RootView.swift, Features/Overview/OverviewView.swift, Design/PersonContextSection.swift, Features/Calls/CallDetailView.swift, and Navigation/NavigationShell.swift. Browser pixels, symbols, and interaction states are illustrative; SwiftUI remains authoritative.

components.name: Home calls stopped panel
components.description: Schematic documentation preview, not the actual native implementation. One positive historical Action panel shows Calls stopped, a large numeral, Total, and See calls. It uses the optional persistent stopped total, including review-needed calls; it is not proof of confirmed scams, current protection, or complete recovery of deleted history. It opens recent retained history, which can have fewer records. Zero uses None so far; missing data uses Total unavailable. Real status stays above it. Source: Features/Overview/StoppedCallsCard.swift and Models/Overview.swift. The numeral is synthetic. Browser pixels, symbols, and interaction states are illustrative; SwiftUI remains authoritative.

narrative.overview:
Shield keeps a familiar native iPhone appearance: grouped lists, straightforward labels, system text, and recognizable controls. Quiet surfaces and four adaptive accents help people find a call, understand its result, and choose the next action. The library metaphor describes legible wayfinding; it does not introduce themed decoration.

The October 12 refinement makes an 80-year-old's understanding the bar. Ordinary screens use everyday words, fewer visible choices, and room for text to grow. Less common details open on request. Setup, disconnection, privacy, and sharing retain the information and explicit confirmations needed for a meaningful choice.
keyCharacteristics: Native tabs, navigation stacks, grouped lists, forms, sheets, menus, and confirmation dialogs.
Action blue, stopped-call red, answered-call teal, and voicemail violet with Light, Dark, and increased-contrast variants.
Semantic Dynamic Type, wrapping text, generous app controls, and content-based stacking.
Explicit person context, sharing scope, truthful service state, and a persistent sample-data marker.
Home's native large title shares the grouped canvas at rest; its collapsed navigation background matches that surface.
One choice per onboarding screen, progressive disclosure, and visible recovery when a task fails.

rules.name: The Outcome Truth Rule
rules.body: Pair color with a familiar outcome label or symbol; a call being checked, offered, or answered never implies an authenticated caller.

rules.name: The Native Type Rule
rules.body: Preserve semantic text styles and allow wrapping or stacking before introducing a fixed text size.

rules.name: The Room for Words Rule
rules.body: Stack metadata and move person context into the page before shrinking text; at accessibility sizes remove decorative row icons when they compete with the label.

rules.name: The Native Surface Rule
rules.body: Use grouped system surfaces and native control feedback before introducing custom elevation or viewport geometry.

rules.name: The Historical Count Rule
rules.body: Use the persistent stopped total, include review-needed calls honestly, and keep it distinct from recent retained history and current protection status; unavailable data is never zero or a weekly fallback.

rules.name: The Recoverable State Rule
rules.body: Name loading, unsaved, unavailable, and failed states in words; offer a visible recovery action and never turn a failed read into a claim that data is empty or protection is active.

rules.name: The Visible Context Rule
rules.body: Show the viewed person and sharing scope in words, and keep participant ownership distinct from helper access.

rules.name: The Explicit Confirmation Rule
rules.body: Keep the action and the proof separate: returning from another app never confirms a carrier or Phone-setting change, and ending a call test never disconnects the phone.

dos: Do use ShieldTheme's adaptive role colors, opaque supporting text, and native grouped system surfaces.
Do pair outcome color with familiar words and SF Symbols while preserving uncertainty.
Do keep semantic Dynamic Type, wrapping text, content-based stacking, 52-point shared app action minima, and 60-point grouped-row defaults.
Do give ordinary tasks one clear next action and reveal less common detail on request.
Do make switches tappable through their labeled row and keep one native accessibility toggle representation.
Do stack call and message metadata from `.xxxLarge` and keep person context in the scrollable page at accessibility sizes.
Do name unsaved changes and failed loads, and place a visible retry or save action beside the relevant task.
Do show playback progress with elapsed and total time, clear pause/resume labels, and a visible Start over action.
Do make person context, message permission, and sample-only state visible in words.
Do retain explicit privacy, sharing, setup, and disconnection confirmations.
Do label the Home count as the persistent historical total, keep real status above it, and distinguish zero, unavailable data, and recent retained history.
Do verify the running native app in Light and Dark Mode, increased contrast, large Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, and Reduced Motion before claiming accessibility approval.
donts: Don't describe a checked, offered, or answered caller as verified, authenticated, or safe.
Don't infer active call checks from stale, missing, paused, or expired status.
Don't promote old tab labels or fixed Surface asset colors from earlier designs into new screens.
Don't present Calls stopped as confirmed scams, complete recovery of already-deleted history, or evidence that current call checks are on.
Don't treat schematic sidecar HTML/CSS as a native pixel specification.
Don't treat helper access as ownership or extend message access implicitly.
Don't present sample summaries, synthetic speech, or temporary keeping as real-message services.
Don't use a failed load as an empty-state, saved-choice, or active-protection claim.
Don't treat an app return, call-test completion, sign-out, or app deletion as confirmation that forwarding is disconnected.
Don't claim a clean native audit, real VoiceOver approval, older-person usability, deployment, or real-call evidence from source extraction or simulator captures.
